lines.text: Since we never met, here's a thing I'm not asking you.
Rime shards. Those slivers the little frost lights leave lying about. I'll take any you've got at the going rate. But three, brought special, I'd pay proper for.
You've a great appetite for something that won't melt.
No questions. That's the arrangement.
I don't recall asking one.
See? You're a natural.
Ah. I can feel those from here. Three, was it?
He counts them into a flat tin without looking. The tin is nearly full. It ought to be white with frost, holding that much cold. It isn't.
You've a lot of those.
No questions, we said.
So we did.
Eldwin looks at the tin a moment longer than he needs to, and says nothing more.
Pleasure. We never met.

choice.text: You look like you've something else not to tell me.

lines.text: There's a cart come up the notch road. A tailor, of a kind. Doesn't stay anywhere long, and doesn't ask where a thing has been.
Last I heard it had stopped in the Woodlot, on the way to the sugar trees.
Last I heard it had stopped by the Coffin Rest, on the old lane. Not a place folk linger, which would suit.
Last I heard it had stopped in the South Fields, off the lane.
And why would you tell me that?
Those little things you carry about. They aren't only money, if you know who to ask.
We never met. Neither did you and the cart.
